title: Unit – 1 : Session – 5 : SLO – 1 | Classify Paradigms
sections: 1) Classification: Java → imperative, object-oriented (with functional features). Prolog → declarative, logic programming. SQL → declarative, database/query. Python → multi-paradigm: imperative, object-oriented, functional.

2) Feature table — Imperative: explicit steps & state changes (Java loops, Python). Declarative: describes what, not how (SQL SELECT). Logic: facts + rules + inference (Prolog parent/ancestor rules). Functional: pure functions, immutability, higher-order functions (Java streams, Python map/lambda).

3) Hierarchical relationship: Programming paradigms divide into Imperative (how: procedural, object-oriented, parallel) and Declarative (what: functional, logic, database/query). Each sub-paradigm refines the parent style — e.g., OOP is imperative with encapsulated state; logic and functional are declarative specializations.
